items.content_text:
CPD Investigating Deadly Crash Involving a Pedestrian on Shallowford Road
 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a crash that resulted in a pedestrian's death Monday afternoon.
 At approximately 11:00 a.m., CPD's Traffic Unit responded to a crash involving a pedestrian in the 7500 block of Shallowford Road. Preliminary findings indicate the pedestrian, a 65-year-old woman, was attempting to cross the road and stepped in front of a vehicle. The driver attempted to swerve, but still hit the pedestrian.
 Hamilton County EMS responded and transported the woman to the hospital where she was pronounced dead. 
 This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.
 #CPDnews

 The Power C Tour is UTC’s statewide outreach effort to connect directly with high school students, transfer students, graduate students and their families in their own communities. At each stop, visitors can meet with representatives from UTC academic colleges and student services, talk with current students and learn more about the opportunities and support available at the University.
 Each event will run from 6-7:30 p.m. and include information booths, light refreshments, prizes and an opportunity to enter a drawing for UTC scholarships.
 🔗  Learn more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/the-road-to-utc-starts-here-power-c…/

This weekend, the HCSO was proud to serve as a presenting sponsor of the 5th Annual Running Down Recidivism 5k, benefiting @thebraveeffect, a Chattanooga nonprofit that provides resources and support to those who have been incarcerated.
 The BRAVE Effect was founded by Joe Jenkins, whose own journey began with incarceration at the Hamilton County Jail and later included several years in the federal prison system. Now, he dedicates his life to empowering and supporting others as they re-enter society.
 We want to thank everyone who participated in and supported this year’s fundraiser as we work together to break the cycle of recidivism. 👟

Before you decide mountain biking "isn't for you," we need to clear a few things up. 👀🚲
 You do NOT need your own mountain bike.
 You do NOT need experience.
 You do NOT need to show up ready to ride singletrack.
 You don't even need to know what half the parts of a mountain bike are called.
 That's what Trail Quest is for.
 Field FUNdamentals starts with the basics in a controlled environment at Greenway Farm, where you can practice things like braking, shifting, balance, body position and bike control before ever taking those skills onto a trail.
 Bike and helmet reservations are available, classes are just $10, and beginners are very much invited.
 All you really need is a pair of closed-toed shoes and a willingness to try something new.
 🗓Tuesdays through November 3
 📍Greenway Farm
 🎟Register at outdoorchattanooga.com/calendar
 Come see what all the mountain biking hype is about!

 Hamilton County, TN – On the late evening of September 18, 2026, HCSO deputies were notified of a social media video showing a male juvenile abusing a dog.
 The investigation led to deputies apprehending the suspect, and he was transported to the Juvenile Detention Center and faces the following charge: 
 • Cruelty to Animals
 Animal services responded to the residence, and an adult family member kept the dog; animal services will follow up on the dog’s condition.
 “We want to thank the public for bringing this disgusting video of a male juvenile brutally abusing a dog to our attention. Our deputies acted swiftly to this abuse, investigating and taking the suspect into custody. Animal cruelty has no place in Hamilton County. If you cannot treat animals with compassion, you do not deserve to have them,” stated Sheriff Austin Garrett.
 This investigation is ongoing, and no further details are available.

items.content_text:
Where are tomorrow's scientists and innovators being trained? 
 Launched this week at the #OECD Blue Sky Forum, our latest Research and Innovation Careers Observatory report provides insights on the people who drive research and innovation forward.
 Some key findings include:
 ➡️ Demand for STI talent is rising fast. Science and engineering professionals grew from 3.2% to 3.7% of total employment across OECD countries between 2015 and 2024.
 ➡️Talent pipelines remain strong. OECD countries awarded over 300,000 new doctoral degrees and 3.9 million master's degrees in 2023.
 ➡️Close to 480,000 doctorates and over 7 million master's degrees were awarded in 2023 across the OECD, as well as OECD accession, partner and EU countries.
 ➡️Talent is concentrated in a few hubs: the EU, China, India, the UK and the US.  Together, these five areas account for 70% of doctoral graduates and over 80% of master's graduates across OECD and EU member, accession and partner economies.
 As countries compete for research talent, understanding where researchers and scientists are being trained and where they are going next will be key to shaping policies on mobility and career development.
 🔗 https://brnw.ch/21x5Oud

items.content_text:
Another pandemic is not a question of if, but when.
 Without effective action, a future pandemic could cause GDP to fall by up to 16.2% in just nine months, new OECD modelling across 51 countries shows.
 But acting early matters. A layered approach with measures such as hand hygiene, masks, ventilation, voluntary quarantine teleworking and domestic travel restrictions could prevent vast majority of deaths, while limiting the economic damage to around 2.5% of GDP. 
 Relying on lockdowns as a last resort, without earlier preventive measures, is both less effective at saving lives and more damaging to the economy.
 Read more: https://brnw.ch/21x5O6P

But acting early matters. A layered approach with measures such as hand hygiene, masks, ventilation, voluntary quarantine teleworking and domestic travel restrictions could prevent vast majority of deaths, while limiting the economic damage to around 2.5% of GDP.
Relying on lockdowns as a last resort, without earlier preventive measures, is both less effective at saving lives and more damaging to the economy.

items.content_text:
Today, we joined EPB and IonQ for the launch of the IonQ Forte Enterprise quantum computer at the EPB Quantum Center, another major step in our community’s emergence as a hub for quantum technology.
 As this industry grows, we’re making sure our students grow with it. From the new Energy and Quantum Industries Academy at Franklin Roberts Future Ready Center to early exposure through TN QuantumWorks, Hamilton County students are gaining pathways to prepare for careers in advanced energy, broadband, cybersecurity, and quantum technology.
 No other community in the region is doing this quite like Hamilton County, developing local talent while attracting people from across America who want to be part of the momentum happening here.

items.title: 🌿💐 Welcome to Red Bank, Malin Flowers & Gifts! 💐🌿 There’s a beautiful new shop in town, and it’s one you’ll want to...
items.content_text:
🌿💐 Welcome to Red Bank, Malin Flowers & Gifts! 💐🌿
 There’s a beautiful new shop in town, and it’s one you’ll want to step inside and experience for yourself.
 On September 3rd, Erin officially opened the doors to Malin Flowers & Gifts, a thoughtfully designed shop filled with fresh blooms, Scandinavian-inspired flowers and gifts, and beautifully curated goods.
 The space itself is quaint, inviting, and full of thoughtful details — but one of the most unique features is the “Gathering Wall.” 🌸
 The idea is simple: gather what speaks to you.
 Whether you're looking for a Gesture, Moment, Gathering, or Home bouquet, the wall gives you a simple way to create something beautiful, even if you’ve never known quite what to choose for a bouquet. Find the colors, textures, and blooms that catch your eye, follow the “recipe,” and create a bouquet that feels like you. And if you’d rather leave the arranging to Erin, there are beautiful premade bouquets ready to go, too. 💐
 And then there’s the “Thrift” shelf — a collection of vases Erin has personally thrifted. Find one you love, take it home with your flowers, and bring the vase back the next time you need a bouquet for a discounted fee. What a lovely way to give something old a new life. 🤍
 And don’t leave without trying the Cardamom Shortbread Cookies made especially for Malin by Cohutta Provisions. 🍪 They’re the perfect little treat to enjoy while taking in all the beautiful things around you.
 From fresh flowers and thoughtfully selected gifts to handcrafted 3D cards, cookbooks, candles, and more, Malin Flowers & Gifts is the kind of place where you can find something special for someone you love — or simply something beautiful for yourself.
 🌿 Fresh blooms. Thoughtful gifts. Beautiful gatherings.
 📍 Find Malin Flowers & Gifts
 3890 Dayton Blvd
 Chattanooga, TN 37415
 🕙 Hours: Tuesday–Saturday, 10 AM–6 PM
 We’re so happy to welcome Erin and Malin Flowers & Gifts to the Red Bank community. Be sure to stop in, explore the Gathering Wall, find a vase you love, and discover all the little treasures tucked inside.
 💐 Welcome to Red Bank, Malin! 🤍

Today is International #EqualPayDay.   
 Women working full time across OECD countries still earn, on average, only 90 cents for every dollar or euro earned by men, reflecting a gender wage gap of around 10%.  
 At the current pace of change, achieving equal pay could still take decades.  
 Pay transparency tools have emerged as a promising approach for addressing gender pay gaps by helping to identify pay disparities and support fairer pay practices.   
 To learn more, join our upcoming event on pay transparency and pay equity:

🚨🚛 IMPORTANT TRASH COLLECTION NOTICE 🚛🚨
 Starting Monday, September 21, 2026, the City of Red Bank will no longer collect garbage from trash cans that were NOT issued by the City.
 Beginning Monday, Public Works staff will place notices on non-City-issued trash cans throughout the community.
 🗑️ Please check your trash can this week! Make sure you are using a City-issued trash can to avoid any interruption in garbage collection.
 Need an extra trash can?
 If your household needs additional capacity, you can request a second City-issued trash can by:
 ✅ Visiting the Red Bank City Hall at 3105 Dayton Blvd to pay for an additional can. Price is $75.00. 
 This change will help provide consistent, safe, and efficient collection services while preventing potential damage to privately owned trash cans during collection.
 📞 Questions? Call Red Bank City Hall at (423) 877-1103.
 ♻️ Thank you for helping us keep Red Bank clean, safe, and beautiful! ♻️
